LESSON: PROJECT

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Tools and production
Topic 4.3: Project
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 20

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Project, part of Tools and production in Grade 9 PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How are skills acquired in Pre- Technical Studies used to solve problems in the community?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify a problem in the locality that can be solved using the skills acquired in Pre-Technical Studies,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Project in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. select an item that can be made to solve the identified problem,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Project in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. make an item to solve the problem identified using locally available materials,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Project in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. utilise skills acquired in Pre-Technical Studies to solve problems in day-to- day life.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Project in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify a problem in the locality that can be solved using the skills acquired in Pre-Technical Studies,

   Project helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. select an item that can be made to solve the identified problem,

   Project helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. make an item to solve the problem identified using locally available materials,

   Project helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. utilise skills acquired in Pre-Technical Studies to solve problems in day-to- day life.

   Project helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. explore the locality to identify problems that can be solved using the skills acquired in Pre-Technical Studies,

2. brainstorm on the possible solutions to the identified problems,

3. use print or digital media to search for information on possible items to solve the identified problem,

4. discuss possible items that can be made to solve the identified problem,

5. select one item that can be made using the skills acquired to solve the identified problem,

6. sketch the item to be made using the skills acquired to solve the identified problem,

7. estimating the cost of materials for making the project item,

8. use locally available materials and tools to make the identified item,

9. estimate the cost to determine the price for the item,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. explore the locality to identify problems that can be solved using the skills acquired in Pre-Technical Studies,
2. brainstorm on the possible solutions to the identified problems,
3. use print or digital media to search for information on possible items to solve the identified problem,
4. discuss possible items that can be made to solve the identified problem,
5. select one item that can be made using the skills acquired to solve the identified problem,
6. sketch the item to be made using the skills acquired to solve the identified problem,
7. estimating the cost of materials for making the project item,
8. use locally available materials and tools to make the identified item,
9. estimate the cost to determine the price for the item,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Project together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: learner develops evaluation and decision making skills when selecting an item that

can be made using the skills acquired.

• Creativity and Imagination: learner experiments with ideas when discussing possible items that can be made to solve the

identified problem.

Values:
• Responsibility: learner cares for tools and materials when making the item.

• Respect: learner appreciates diverse opinions when discussing possible items that can be made to solve the identified

problem.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Environmental Conservation: learner conserves natural resources when using locally available materials and tools to make

the project item.

• Financial Literacy: learner enhances budgeting skills when estimating the cost of materials for making the project item.

Link to other Subjects:

Creative Arts and Sports: learner enhances drawing skills when sketching the project item.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. identify a problem in the locality that can be solved using the skills acquired in Pre-Technical Studies,
2. select an item that can be made to solve the identified problem,
3. make an item to solve the problem identified using locally available materials,
4. utilise skills acquired in Pre-Technical Studies to solve problems in day-to- day life.

Remember the key question: How are skills acquired in Pre- Technical Studies used to solve problems in the community?
